title: A right adjoint of an exact functor preserves K-injective complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and let $u:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $v:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be additive functors with $u$ right adjoint to $v$ and $v$ exact. Call a cochain complex $I$ of $\mathcal A$ *K-injective* if every morphism of complexes $M\to I$ from an acyclic complex $M$ (all cohomology objects zero) is homotopic to zero, i.e. $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(M,I)=0$ in the homotopy category for every acyclic $M$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] (equivalently, the Hom complex $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(M,I)$ is acyclic for every acyclic $M$, as in [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], since $H^n\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(M,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(M[-n],I)$ and shifts of acyclic complexes are acyclic). Then for every K-injective complex $I$ of $\mathcal A$ the complex $u(I)=(u(I^r),u(d^r))_r$ obtained by applying $u$ termwise is a K-injective complex of $\mathcal B$.
